module.purpose: Defines the tldraw video shape utility and its rendered video component, including shape defaults, asset creation, SVG export, editing behavior, and browser media presentation.
module.summary: This module integrates video assets with tldraw's shape system. It supplies metadata and migration bindings, creates shapes from video assets, exports a representative video frame to SVG, and renders an HTML video element with loading, fullscreen, editing, reduced-motion, accessibility, and broken-asset handling. Rendering is coordinated through editor hooks and cached asynchronous media conversion.
module.businessContext: Supports video content creation and editing in the collaborative whiteboard product. Failures affect video placement, playback, accessibility, editing controls, and exported document previews.

detail.summary: VideoShapeUtil defines the video shape type, schema metadata, default options, and shape-level integration surface for editing, rendering, asset creation, indicators, accessibility, and SVG export.

specLiterals.role: Identifies this shape utility's registered shape type and handled asset type.

units.name: getDefaultProps

detail.name: getDefaultProps
preconditions: The VideoShapeUtil instance has an options object with an autoplay value.
postconditions: Returns a TLVideoShape props object with w and h set to 100.
Returns assetId as null, url as an empty string, and altText as an empty string.
Returns time as 0 and playing as true.
invariants: The returned object contains exactly the default video-shape properties defined by this method.
The method does not mutate instance state or external state.
edgeCases: The configured autoplay value is propagated unchanged, including falsey values.
The default assetId is null when no asset is assigned.
The default URL and alt text are empty strings.
detail.summary: Returns the default property set for a video shape, including its dimensions, asset reference, playback settings, metadata, and initial playback state.

specLiterals.role: Default width and height for a video shape.
Default playing state for a video shape.

specTests.then: It returns props with w and h equal to 100, assetId equal to null, autoplay equal to false, url and altText equal to empty strings, time equal to 0, and playing equal to true.

units.name: createShapeForAsset

detail.name: createShapeForAsset
detail.signature: override createShapeForAsset(asset: TLAsset, position: VecModel): TLShapePartial | null
preconditions: asset must provide the video asset identifier and width and height properties expected by TLVideoAsset.
position must provide numeric x and y coordinates.
postconditions: Returns a non-null partial shape object with type 'video'.
The returned shape's x and y equal position.x and position.y.
The returned props contain assetId from the asset, and w and h from the asset's video properties.
The returned shape id is generated by createShapeId().
invariants: The returned shape type is always 'video'.
The asset dimensions are copied without transformation.
edgeCases: A video asset with zero or otherwise boundary dimensions produces a shape carrying those dimensions unchanged.
The method performs no runtime asset-kind validation; malformed asset data may produce undefined property values or a runtime property-access error.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: No explicit validation or fallback is performed; malformed inputs are propagated into the result or can cause a runtime property-access error.

detail.summary: Creates a partial video shape for a video asset at the supplied position. The shape carries a generated identifier, the video asset dimensions, and full opacity.

specLiterals.role: Shape type discriminator for the returned partial shape.
Fixed opacity assigned to newly created video shapes.

specTests.when: createShapeForAsset is called with the asset and position.
specTests.then: It returns a non-null shape of type 'video' with x 10, y 20, opacity 1, props { assetId: 'asset-1', w: 640, h: 360 }, and a generated id.

units.name: getIndicatorPath

detail.name: getIndicatorPath
preconditions: shape.props.w and shape.props.h are available as rectangle dimensions.
postconditions: The returned path contains a rectangle whose origin is (0, 0), width is shape.props.w, and height is shape.props.h.
invariants: The indicator rectangle is anchored at the local origin.
The rectangle dimensions are taken directly from shape.props.w and shape.props.h.
edgeCases: Zero width or height produces a degenerate rectangle with the corresponding zero dimension.
Negative width or height is passed directly to Path2D.rect without normalization.

raises: Any runtime error thrown by Path2D construction or rect when the execution environment does not support them.
errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: No explicit validation or fallback is performed.

detail.summary: Creates and returns a rectangular Path2D indicator covering the video shape's full width and height.

specLiterals.role: Defines the rectangle's local x and y origin.

specTests.when: getIndicatorPath is called with the shape.
specTests.then: It returns a Path2D containing a rectangle at (0, 0) with width 320 and height 180.

units.name: toSvg

detail.name: toSvg
preconditions: shape.props is available and contains the video shape properties.
ctx.resolveAssetUrl can resolve an asset URL for a referenced asset.
postconditions: When export succeeds, returns an image element whose href is the captured frame data URL and whose width and height match shape.props.w and shape.props.h.
The returned image element has an aria-label equal to shape.props.altText.
When required asset or frame data is unavailable, returns null.
invariants: The video frame is captured at time 0.
The exported image dimensions are taken directly from shape.props.w and shape.props.h.
Asset frame results are obtained through videoSvgExportCache.
edgeCases: If shape.props.assetId is absent or falsy, returns null without attempting asset lookup.
If the editor has no asset for shape.props.assetId, returns null.
If asset URL resolution returns a falsy value, returns null without loading a video.
If video frame extraction returns a falsy value, returns null.
If asset lookup, cache retrieval, URL resolution, video loading, or frame extraction rejects, the rejection propagates to the caller.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Missing or unusable asset-related data produces null; rejected asynchronous dependencies propagate their errors.
errorPolicy.returnsOnError: null for missing assetId, missing asset, unresolved asset URL, or missing frame data

detail.ioFormatSpec: Returns null or an image element equivalent to <image href={src} width={shape.props.w} height={shape.props.h} aria-label={shape.props.altText} />. The href is a video frame data URL captured at time 0.
detail.summary: Converts a video shape with a resolvable asset into an SVG image containing a captured video frame. Returns null when the shape has no asset, the asset cannot be found, the asset URL cannot be resolved, or no frame data is produced.

specLiterals.role: Specifies the video timestamp at which the exported frame is captured.

specTests.then: It resolves to null and does not require an asset lookup.
It resolves to an image element using the frame data URL, the shape width and height, and the shape altText.

units.name: VideoShape

detail.name: VideoShape
preconditions: shape is a valid TLVideoShape with an id and props containing assetId, w, autoplay, and altText.
The component is rendered within the editor context required by its hooks.
postconditions: The rendered shape exposes an HTML video element when an asset URL is available.
The video is muted, looped, inline-playing, non-draggable, and configured to disable remote playback and picture-in-picture.
The video is focused when the shape is editing and the video has loaded.
invariants: The video source is keyed by its resolved URL.
The video is hidden until loaded unless editing causes its pointer events to be enabled.
Autoplay is enabled only when shape.props.autoplay is true and reduced motion is not preferred.
Editing controls are enabled only while editing and when the shape width multiplied by efficient zoom is at least 110.
Fullscreen state reflects whether the rendered video is the document fullscreen element.
A loading spinner is shown while a resolved video URL has not yet loaded when Spinner is available.
edgeCases: When no asset is available, renders a BrokenAssetIcon instead of a video.
When an asset exists without a source and Spinner is available, renders the Spinner.
When an asset URL is unavailable, renders neither a video nor a spinner in the URL branch.
When video loaded data fires, marks the video as loaded and removes its loading state.
When reduced motion is preferred, autoplay is disabled even if shape.props.autoplay is true.
When the shape is not being edited, video controls are disabled and the video is hidden until loaded.
When the video is already the active document element during editing, it is not refocused.
stateMutations: Local isLoaded state changes to true on the video's loadeddata event.
Local isFullscreen state tracks fullscreenchange events.
The video element receives focus while editing after it is loaded.
A fullscreenchange listener is registered on the video owner document or editor container document and removed on cleanup.
detail.ioFormatSpec: Returns JSX containing an HTMLContainer with a video element whose source is the resolved asset URL. The video uses width="100%", height="100%", muted, loop, playsInline, autoPlay conditional on autoplay and reduced-motion preference, controls conditional on editing and zoomed size, and aria-label from shape.props.altText.
detail.summary: Renders a video shape with asset loading, playback, editing controls, loading and broken-asset states, and fullscreen tracking. The video is focused while its shape is being edited and controls are shown only when the shape is sufficiently large at the current zoom.

specLiterals.role: Minimum width-times-efficient-zoom threshold for showing editing controls.
CSS class pattern identifying the video shape instance.
CSS class applied while the video is the fullscreen element.
Base CSS class applied to rendered videos.
Text color used by the shape container.
Fallback background color used when no loaded video is present.
Fallback border used when no loaded video is present.

specTests.when: The component renders while the shape is being edited.
specTests.then: It renders the video with autoplay enabled, controls enabled, the resolved URL as its source, and pointer events enabled.

specTests.when: The component renders outside editing mode.
specTests.then: The video is hidden and a Spinner is rendered when Spinner is available.
It renders BrokenAssetIcon instead of a video element.
